Facet Parameters from a Many-Facet Rasch Model

Source: R/facet_parameters.R
facet_parameters.Rd

Extracts the measures of a third facet, for example raters, from a many-facet Rasch model fitted with brms, with posterior summaries, the number of ratings, the observed average rating and a fair average rating for each element.

Usage

facet_parameters(
  model,
  facet_var,
  item_var = item,
  person_var = id,
  draws = FALSE,
  prob = 0.95
)

Arguments

model

A fitted brmsfit object from a many-facet model with the facet as a random intercept, a fixed effect, or a threshold group. Examples:

Rating scale, random raters

rating ~ 1 + item + (1 | rater) + (1 | id), family = acat.

Partial credit by item

rating | thres(gr = item) ~ 1 + (1 | rater) + (1 | id).

Rater-specific rating scales

rating | thres(gr = rater) ~ 1 + item + (1 | id).

Dichotomous

y ~ 1 + item + (1 | rater) + (1 | id), family = bernoulli().

facet_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the facet, for example rater.

item_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the items. Default is item.

person_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the persons. Default is id.

draws

Logical. If TRUE, the centred posterior draws of the facet locations are included as a matrix (elements x draws). Default is FALSE.

prob

Numeric in \((0, 1)\). Width of the highest density continuous interval (HDCI). Default is 0.95.

Value

A list with the following elements:

summary

A tibble with one row per facet element and the columns: the facet variable, n (number of ratings), observed_avg (mean observed rating), fair_avg, fair_avg_lower and fair_avg_upper (posterior mean and HDCI of the fair average, see Details), location (posterior mean location, positive = lower ratings), se (posterior SD), hdci_lower, hdci_upper and n_eff (bulk effective sample size).

thresholds

(Only with thres(gr = facet)) A tibble with one row per element and threshold: the facet variable, threshold, location, se, hdci_lower and hdci_upper, on the same scale as summary. NULL otherwise.

facet_sd

(Only for a random facet) A tibble with the posterior mean, SD and HDCI of the facet standard deviation. NULL otherwise.

draws_matrix

(Only if draws = TRUE) A numeric matrix of centred location draws with one row per element and one column per posterior draw.

Details

Locations. The model is read as \(\theta_v - \delta_i - \lambda_j\) on the logit scale, where \(\delta_i\) is the item location and \(\lambda_j\) the location of facet element \(j\). A positive location means lower ratings, so for raters it is severity, on the same side as item difficulty in item_parameters. The locations are centred within each posterior draw so that they average 0. The result is the same whether the facet is a random effect or a fixed effect with any contrasts, including contr_sum_zero. With facet-specific thresholds (thres(gr = rater)) the location is the mean of the element's thresholds, and the thresholds table shows each threshold. brms sets the number of thresholds per element from the categories that element used, so set it in the formula, as in thres(3, gr = rater) for four categories. The function stops if the elements have different numbers of thresholds. Widely spaced thresholds for a rater mean the middle categories cover a wide range of locations and are used often (central tendency). Closely spaced thresholds mean the extreme categories are used often.

Fair average. The observed average rating of a rater depends on which persons and items the rater happened to rate. The fair average is the expected rating the element would give a person at the mean location of the persons in the sample, averaged over the items, computed in each posterior draw. It corresponds to the "Fair-M average" of the Facets program. Person x facet (halo) effects are set to 0. Ratings are on the scale brms uses: 0 and 1 for bernoulli(), categories 1 to \(C\) for ordinal families.

Reliability. With draws = TRUE, the draws matrix can be passed to RMUreliability. For raters, a high value means that the raters differ reliably in severity, which is a problem for the ratings, not a sign of their quality. With few elements, for example 3 to 5 raters, the correlation across elements that RMU is based on is very uncertain.

References

Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-facet Rasch measurement. MESA Press.

Eckes, T. (2015). Introduction to many-facet Rasch measurement: Analyzing and evaluating rater-mediated assessments (2nd ed.). Peter Lang.

See also

item_parameters, contr_sum_zero, infit_statistic (with facet_var), RMUreliability.

Examples

# \donttest{
library(brms)

# Simulated ratings: 60 persons, 3 items, 4 raters, two raters per person
set.seed(1)
d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:60, function(p) {
  expand.grid(id = p, item = c("i1", "i2", "i3"),
              rater = paste0("R", c((p - 1) %% 4 + 1, p %% 4 + 1)),
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
severity <- c(R1 = -0.5, R2 = 0, R3 = 0.2, R4 = 0.6)
theta <- rnorm(60)
d$y <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, plogis(theta[d$id] - severity[d$rater]))

fit <- brm(y ~ 1 + item + (1 | rater) + (1 | id), data = d,
           family = bernoulli(), chains = 2, iter = 1000)
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Error in .fun(model_code = .x1): Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')

fp <- facet_parameters(fit, facet_var = rater, draws = TRUE)
#> Error: object 'fit' not found
fp$summary
#> Error: object 'fp' not found
RMUreliability(fp$draws_matrix)
#> Error: object 'fp' not found
# }
